A big reason I created this subverse was because my wife and I have disagreements pretty regularly, and I've always wanted a third-party present that wasn't a friend to either of us. So here is a big one we had/are currently having.

The Situation: Last week I was invited by a few friends from my new job to come out with them to celebrate one of their birthdays. The original plan was to meet at the Beef O'Brady's near our work in time to watch the Lightning vs Blackhawks game. I tell my wife the plan, and she lets me go. We arrive at Beef's and it is PACKED with a 45-minute wait for the next available table. So the guy whose birthday it is calls and makes a reservation at a Winghouse down the street. He tells us there is a table ready, and we head over there. We had some wings and watched the game, and each had a beer. I get home, and my wife asks where I ended up eating. I had no intentions of lying or hiding where I ate so I just said Winghouse. The argument begins....

The Stakes: If I win, I may be able to go out with my guy friends on a semi-regular basis. If I lose, Winghouse and Hooters are out of the question for places I am allowed to go. My wife and I have agreed that this will be the deciding factor. Please take it seriously and handle it while remaining totally unbiased.

Wife's Argument: She's uncomfortable with it. It's disrespectful for me to go if she's not comfortable. The women at Winghouse are only there to flirt and get stared at by men. Men are only there to flirt with and stare at the girls. She "knows I looked at all those girls with big tits and fat asses" because why else would I go? She believes men must go for the women because otherwise they would just go to any other sports bar. When I argued that our waitress didn't have big boobs or much of a butt, she said it was evidence that I was obviously looking (which is technically true I suppose.) She also brought up the fact that I asked her not to work there when she had the opportunity because I didn't like the way they objectified women (also true.)

My Argument: I didn't originally agree to go to Winghouse, I signed up for Beef O'Brady's. I concede that most men who go to Winghouse or Hooters do go there for the... perks, but I maintain that I am simply not one of those guys. Out of the 10 men I went with, only 2 ever made immature comments, and the jokes weren't met with much laughter. I was there for the game, and paid attention to that and the conversations being had with my coworkers. I think my wife should entrust in me to be mature and mentally faithful no matter where I am, but understand how this could make her uncomfortable. I think it's very important to make friends with the people you work with, and that going out with them every now and then would make work a much more social and therefore bearable experience. The guys liked the food and suggested going every Wednesday.

So... Should I be able to go to Winghouse with my Coworkers?
Me, My Wife, and the Hooters/Winghouse Argument!

My voat is with the husband.

First off being "allowed to go" better just be the way you put it, because being allowed is what children and pets get. You're both adults capable of acting in such a way.

To the point now. Nobody was going out to pick up women or flirt (and if you were knock it the fuck off), so it doesn't matter what those girls are wearing. You're going to run into attractive people no matter where you go, it doesn't mean you're trying to shack up. And acting like either of you don't notice attractive people of the opposite sex is a lie. What is good is when you can see people you find incredibly physically attractive and still go home to the spouse you love because you have more than that. So go out and look, both of you, but do it knowing what you have makes you happy.

I'd listen to the wife. As long as she's not policing your every move and making you get approval to hang out with people, there's nothing to suggest she's being anything but reasonably uncomfortable with you going to a business that provides soft sexual services. Ignore her feelings and you risk driving a wedge and causing emotional distance.

If you've explained things to her and she's still uncomfortable, I'd respect her feelings. It's it worth making her feel inadequate or insecure just to spend more time with friends?

I made a similar mistake and hurt my relationship a lot. My partner was uncomfortable with me spending hours daily at university with someone I regarded as a friend. I denied that anything was going on and kept working with the person. Even if it hadn't turned it that my partner was right (that friend started making advances and made it abundantly clear what they wanted), I think that ignoring their feelings would have done most of the damage we've suffered.

When dealing with your husband or wife, err on the side of respecting their feelings and you'll be happy.

I'm also with the husband on this one.

Sports bars are generally a very strong "dudes atmosphere" no matter where you go. A place like Winghouse is just being shameless in that. Sure, it's sexist, but other than that it's just a restaurant.

It would be one thing if you were going out to a strip club, but you want to a restaurant. The wife here should understand that. Yes, there will be women with their tits bursting out. But so what? You could run into that anywhere. At least you're mentally prepared for it. As an adult, you can act mature and enjoy the food and the game without being unfaithful or otherwise wronging your spouse.

That being said, I see where the wife is coming from. It is something that the husband should fully expect to make the wife uncomfortable. But she should be able to trust you to not be focused on other women's bodies. You're married, after all. On the internet, full on porn is never more than three clicks away, but she doesn't feel uncomfortable while you're on the computer.

Tl;Dr you're there to watch a game and enjoy dinner with some friends. The restaurant shouldn't matter. If it helps, maybe take the wife with you on the next trip so she can see firsthand that you're just enjoying a couple beers with the guys?
